text.first-impression: Gye, people meet you and feel oddly understood. You're gentle, observant, a little mysterious, with soft energy that makes people relax without knowing why. Ten seconds in, you've picked up their mood and matched it. They feel like you get them. You do. What they don't see: you've also absorbed their stress, and you'll carry it home like a souvenir nobody asked you to buy. You're basically a sponge in a nice jumper, and you go home much heavier than you arrived. Wring yourself out before bed. Seriously, every night.
text.your-red-flag: Your red flag: you're vague. Maybe. We'll see. Whatever you want. You hint instead of asking, then feel hurt when nobody picks up on the hint. You also retreat into your imagination when life gets hard, which is cosy but isn't a plan. And you can be a bit secretive, sharing the weather report but never the forecast. Mystery is charming on a first date. By month six, it's just confusing, and the people who love you are tired of guessing. Give them the forecast. They can handle it, I promise.
text.how-you-sabotage-love: In love you're tender, intuitive, deeply romantic, the partner who senses something's wrong before a word is said. Beautiful. Your sabotage is expecting that same skill in return. If they loved me, they'd know. They don't know. They're not a weather app. You also sometimes fall for the idea of someone more than the actual person, because your imagination is very generous with the details. Say your needs. In words. Specific ones. Whole sentences, ideally with a verb. Try one this week and watch how relieved they look. Genuinely relieved.
text.friends-and-work: At work you're creative and perceptive, wonderful with people and good at reading what a client really wants. But you drift when things feel meaningless, and you avoid conflict like it's a wasp at a picnic. With friends you're the empathetic one, the one who just gets it. But you absorb their problems until you're completely drained, then vanish for a week to recover, and nobody knows why you went quiet. Tell them. You're allowed to need a recharge. A simple I need a quiet week, love you, sorts it.
text.the-lie: The lie you tell yourself: I'm just a private person. Sometimes it's privacy. Sometimes it's the fear that if people see the real you, it'll be too much for them. It won't. You also tell yourself that you don't need much. You need a lot, actually, emotionally, and that's completely okay. Needing a lot isn't a flaw. Hiding it and hoping someone will notice is the part that keeps going wrong. Stop hiding it. Start with one person who's earned it. Tell them one real thing. Then breathe. Then do it again next week.
text.the-fix: The fix, because Bom gave me the look. Say one clear sentence about what you want, every single day. Not a hint. A sentence. Protect your energy: leave a room when it's draining you, politely and without guilt. Write your daydreams down, then go and do one real thing in the world. In love, assume they can't read your mind, because they truly can't. You're the rain: quiet, everywhere, life-giving. You're also allowed to simply say it's raining. Out loud. That's the whole fix. Try it today. Once is enough to start.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gye. 'Maybe' is not an answer. It's a fog machine.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Gentle, and expecting everyone to be psychic. They're not.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: You absorb everyone's mood and then vanish for a week.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Yes. Now let them understand you. Use a whole sentence.

spring.intro: Spring Gye, Wood ran your birth season and Water feeds Wood, so you're gentle rain making everyone else bloom. You're kind, intuitive and the best listener in any group. People see someone soft and lovely. Your friends know you'll listen for two hours and share nothing about yourself. Your red flag is invisible giving. You support everyone, then feel resentful that nobody asks about you, but you never let them. In love you nurture quietly and wait to be noticed. At work you help everyone's project succeed and get credit for none. The fix: when someone asks how you are, give a real answer. Two full sentences. Minimum.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They asked how you were and you said 'fine, you?' in one breath. Gye.

summer.intro: Summer Gye, Fire ran your season and Water controls Fire, so you're a small cloud trying to cool a heatwave. You soothe everyone. People see someone calm and agreeable. Your friends know you're a people-pleaser with a secret temper that shows up roughly twice a year. Your red flag is peacekeeping until you evaporate. You say yes, smooth things over, avoid conflict, and then one day you rain on everything at once. In love you swallow small complaints until they become one giant storm. At work you agree in meetings and disagree in your head. The fix: say one small no a day. Keep the rain regular.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You said yes to everything for six months, then cried at a vending machine. Gye.

autumn.intro: Autumn Gye, Metal ran your birth season and Metal generates Water, so your intuition is razor-sharp and you know it. You read people in seconds. People see someone quiet and observant. Your friends know you've already decided who you trust at the party and who's lying about their job. Your red flag is acting on assumptions as if they're facts. You decide what someone meant and respond to that, not to what they said. In love partners get punished for things they only did in your head. At work you're perceptive and occasionally suspicious of everyone. The fix: check your reading with one question before you act on it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You were mad at them for something they did in your imagination. Gye. Come on.

winter.intro: Winter Gye, Water ran your season and doubled your element, so you're mist, snow and dreams. Imaginative, sensitive, living about forty percent in your own head. People see someone gentle and a little mysterious. Your friends know you replied to their message in your head and forgot to actually send it. Your red flag is daydreaming instead of doing. You imagine the conversation, the trip, the career change so vividly that it feels done. In love you fall for the version of them you invented. At work your ideas are gorgeous and still in draft. The fix: turn one daydream into one real step this week. Tiny counts.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your daydreams are beautiful, Gye. Let's give one of them legs.

strength.strong: Strong chart, Gye. Your intuition is so well fed you think you're psychic. You're often right, which makes it worse. The blind spot: you decide what people feel without asking them. You act on your read, get hurt by your read, and nobody else even knew there was a read. In love partners get blamed for subtext they didn't write. With friends you quietly withdraw from people who did nothing wrong. The fix: ask before you assume. Are you annoyed with me takes four seconds and saves four weeks.
strength.weak: Weak chart, Gye, so your rain evaporates easily in strong company. The blind spot: you disappear. You agree, accommodate and adapt until you're a fog in the corner of every room. People call you easygoing. You call it keeping the peace. Nobody calls it what it is, which is hiding. In love you lose your voice inside theirs. At work you have opinions in the shower and none in meetings. The fix: say your opinion first in one conversation this week, before anyone else's. Then hold it.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood. You're all growth, plans and ambition, and you never stop reaching. Cute. Also exhausting. You start projects faster than you finish them, and you think rest is for people with fewer goals. You argue to win rather than to understand. Yeon's prescription: prune. Finish one thing before starting another. Say you're right once a week and mean it. A tree that never stops growing eventually just falls over.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood. Starting things is hard for you, so you just... don't. You wait for the right moment, and the right moment is apparently very busy. You have plans in drafts and ideas in your notes app from three years ago. Yeon's prescription: take the first ugly step today. Send the email. Sign up for the class. Buy the plant. Momentum isn't a mood. It's a decision you make before you feel ready.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire. Everything's urgent, everything's dramatic, and your feelings arrive with sirens on. You're fun and bright, and you're also impulsive, and you've sent messages you'd love to unsend. Yeon's prescription: wait one night before any big decision. Drink water, literally and spiritually. Let your calmest friend talk you down before your wildest one hypes you up. Your spark is great. Your house fires are not.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire. You're lovely, but you're keeping your light on its dimmest setting. You hang back, never celebrate yourself, and assume people won't notice you anyway. That isn't modesty. It's hiding with good manners. Yeon's prescription: be seen. Post the thing, wear the colour, tell the joke out loud. Go outside in the sun. People can't love what they can't see, and you're worth seeing.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth. You're stable. Very stable. Possibly too stable. Same restaurant, same route, same opinion, same worry on repeat. You call it reliable. It's also a rut with nice furniture. Yeon's prescription: one new thing a week. It doesn't have to be big. A new food, a new walk, a new person to talk to. Growth needs a little mess, and you can tidy it up afterwards if it makes you feel better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth. You're a little all over the place. Plans change, meals get skipped, home is wherever you last dropped your bag. You're adaptable, sure, but you never quite feel settled. Yeon's prescription: routine. Boring, beautiful routine. Same bedtime, real meals, one corner of your home that's only yours. Grounded people make better decisions. Yes, I'm looking directly at you.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal. You're sharp, critical, and your opinions come with edges. You decide fast and judge faster. People respect you, and also slightly fear your face in meetings. Yeon's prescription: soften up. Ask before you judge. Let some things stay imperfect. Cry at a film. You can keep your standards and still let people near you without running a full security check first.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal. Boundaries? Never heard of them. You say yes when you mean no, answer messages at midnight, and lend people your time without ever getting it back. Yeon's prescription: one no a week, with no explanation attached. Declutter something. Unsubscribe, unfollow, unclench. A boundary isn't mean. It's just a door with a lock, and you're allowed to own the key.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water. You think. And think. And then think about what you thought. You feel everything and analyse it until it turns to soup. Your intuition is brilliant. Your sleep schedule is not. Yeon's prescription: get out of your head and into your body. Walk, cook, lift something heavy. Put a timer on the overthinking. Then go and live a little.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water. You go, go, go and never stop to feel anything. Rest is for the weak, reflection is a waste of time, and you've been busy for about five years straight. Yeon's prescription: sit still. Ten minutes. No phone. Write one honest line before bed. Your feelings don't disappear because you're running. They just wait for you, patiently, like a bill.

too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood. You started a new life plan on Monday. It's Wednesday. New plan.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: All that drive is wonderful. Finishing one thing will feel even better.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: three dramatic exits from group chats this year. I counted.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion lights rooms up. Count to ten before the big reply.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Heavy Earth: same order, same route, same hoodie since 2019. I see you.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your steadiness makes people feel safe. Try one new thing for fun.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Lots of Metal. Your honesty has made two baristas reconsider their careers.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Your clarity is a gift. Wrap it in a little kindness.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Overflowing Water: you've overthought this reading three times already. Stop.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is beautiful. Come back to shore when it gets heavy.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: No Wood, no ambition. Your five-year plan is 'see what happens'.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood just means growth needs a nudge. One small goal is plenty.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: No Fire. You'd describe your best night out ever as 'fine'. Show some spark!

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire can mute your joy. Do one thing just because it's fun.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: No Earth. You've changed flat, job and hair colour twice this year.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth makes it hard to settle. A simple routine is grounding.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: No Metal. You've never said no to anyone in your life, have you?

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal means boundaries take practice. Start with one tiny no.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: No Water. Someone cried in front of you and you offered a snack.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water can hide feelings. Name one out loud today.
